title: 4　索引在艺术关联域中的套叠
originalTitle: 4　The Involution of the Index in the Art Nexus

zh: 4.1　施动者／受动者关系的层级嵌套
en: 4.1　Hierarchical Embedding of Agent/Patient Relations

zh: 这就完成了我们对二元关系的概览。读者会注意到，在讨论这些关系时，常常有必要提及涉及两个以上项的更复杂关系。这类表达式的一个例子是：
en: This completes our survey of binary relations. As the reader will have noticed, in the discussion of these relations, it has often been necessary to refer to more complicated relations, involving more than two terms. An example of such an expression, would be:

zh: [[[原型-A] → 艺术家-A] → 索引-A] ⟶ 接受者-P。
en: [[[Prototype-A] → Artist-A] → Index-A] ⟶ Recipient-P.

zh: 这一表达式指这样一个施动者—受动者关系关联域：接受者是“受动者”，作用于他的施动者是索引。这是（次要）施动者（索引）与“首要”受动者（在这个实例中是接受者）之间的关系。我采用这样一个图示约定：始终用长箭头“⟶”表示索引—施动者与关系中“首要”受动者之间的关系，以区别于表示较低层级施动者／受动者关系的短箭头“→”。由于索引的中心地位（见上文3.8），它总是紧靠长箭头的左侧（偶尔在右侧）。施动者总是放在受动者左侧；词尾“-A”和“-P”其实是多余的，因为任何在另一项左侧的项总是被解释为相对于它的“施动者”；然而我保留“-A”和“-P”后缀，因为它们使所得公式更易理解，或至少我希望如此。
en: This expression refers to a nexus of agent patient relationships such that the recipient is the ‘patient' and the agent acting on him is the index. This is the relationship between a (secondary) agent (the index) and a ‘primary' patient, in this instance, the recipient. I adopt the graphic convention of always indicating the relationship between the index-agent and the ‘primary' patient in a relation by the use of a long arrow ‘⟶’ as opposed to the short arrow ‘→’ indicating subordinate agent/patient relations. Because of the centrality of the index (see above, 3.8) it is always immediately to the left (or occasionally to the right) of the long arrow. Agents are always placed to the left of patients; the terminations ‘-A' and ‘-P' are really redundant because any term to the left of another is always interpreted as an ‘agent' with respect to it; however, I retain the ‘-A' and ‘-P' suffixes because they make the resulting formulae more readily intelligible, or at least, I hope they do.

zh: 上述公式中的索引并非自主地作用于接受者。它可能是能动性集中显现的载体，却也在中介其他作用于受动者即接受者的能动性。接受者对索引的反应包含这样一个溯因：索引是“被制造之物”，是艺术家能动性的结果。也就是说，索引相对于接受者是施动者，凭的是接受者从它之中溯因出艺术家的能动性这一事实。索引（相对于接受者）是施动者，但同时相对于它所中介的艺术家能动性又是受动者。接受者作为受动者与艺术家作为施动者之间的这种“间接”关系，在我们的公式中经由方括号表达。“索引”这一项在自身之内包含另一项“艺术家”；于是“[索引]”展开为“[[艺术家] 索引]”。加上“-A”和“-P”后缀，以及表示艺术家相对于索引是施动者的能动性箭头，这就成为：[[艺术家-A] → 索引-A] ⟶ 接受者-P。
en: The index in the above formula is not acting on the recipient autonomously. It may be the focal carrier of agency, but it is serving to mediate other types of agency affecting the patient recipient. The recipient's response to the index incorporates the abduction that the index is a ‘made thing', the outcome of the agency of an artist. That is to say, the index is an agent with respect to the recipient by virtue of the fact that the recipient abducts the agency of the artist from it. The index is an agent (with respect to the recipient) but it is simultaneously a patient, with respect to the agency of the artist, which it mediates. This ‘indirect' relationship between the recipient as patient and the artist as agent is expressed in our formula via the brackets. The term ‘index' includes within itself another term, ‘artist'; thus, ‘[Index]' expands to become ‘[ [Artist] Index]'. Adding ‘-A' and ‘-P' suffixes, and the agency arrow indicating that the artist is an agent with respect to the index, this becomes: [[Artist-A] → Index-A] ⟶ Recipient-P.

zh: 最后，在上述公式中，原型也作为相对于艺术家、索引和接受者的施动者出现。只有当作出艺术家活动从属于原型（例如从属于原型的外貌，如肖像画等写实艺术形式）的溯因时，这才可能发生。从某种观点看，肖像是模特儿外貌的索引，以艺术家制作索引的活动为中介，而索引又把原型的外貌传递给接受者。模特儿的外貌使索引呈现为它所呈现的样子。这通过把原型括在“艺术家”方括号内来表达：“[[艺术家] 索引]”变为“[[[原型] 艺术家] 索引]”，最后加上“-A”和“-P”后缀及能动性箭头，就成为 [[[原型-A] → 艺术家-A] → 索引-A] ⟶ 接受者-P，即我们的出发点。
en: Finally, in the above formula, the prototype also makes an appearance as an agent with respect to the artist, the index, and the recipient. This can only occur when the abduction is made that the activities of the artist are subordinated to the prototype, for example, to the appearance of the prototype, as in realistic forms of art, such as portraiture. From a certain point of view, a portrait is an index of the appearance of the sitter, mediated by the artist's performance in creating an index, which mediates the prototype's appearance to the recipient. The sitter's appearance caused the index to appear as it does. This is expressed by enclosing the prototype in the ‘artist' brackets, ‘[ [Artist] Index]' becomes ‘[[[Prototype] Artist] Index]’, which finally with the addition of the ‘-A' and ‘-P' suffixes, and the agency arrows, becomes [[[Prototype-A] → Artist-A] → Index-A] ⟶ Recipient-P, our starting-point.

zh: 4.2　替换的效果
en: 4.2　The Effect of Substitutions

zh: 这样的公式有什么用？我非常清楚，许多人觉得形式化令人反感，尤其是对艺术事务感兴趣的那类人，他们中许多（事实上像我一样）在学校数学课上吃尽苦头。我敢说，所有这些符号，尽管我已把它们保持到最少并尽可能清晰，似乎与“艺术”关系不大。尽管如此，如果形式化真正有助于清晰思考，那它就有某种意义。我主张，正在讨论的公式以最经济的方式概括了艺术品中介社会关系的无数可能性中的一种。用更印象式的语言说，
en: What purpose does such a formula serve? I am only too well aware that many people find formalization objectionable, especially the kind of people who interest themselves in artistic matters, many of whom (like me, in fact) suffered exceedingly during maths lessons at school. I dare say all these symbols, even though I have kept them to the minimum and made them as perspicuous as possible, seem to have little to do with ‘art'. None the less, there is some point in formalization if it genuinely assists one in thinking clearly. The formula under discussion, I claim, encapsulates in the most economical way, just one of the myriad possibilities which exist for art objects to mediate social relations. In more impressionistic language,

en: picks out the situation in which a ‘passive' spectator is causally affected by the appearance (or other attributes) of a prototype of an artwork (the index), when this attribute is seen as itself causal of the spectator's response. This is a very common situation. A good example of this would be our response to Reynolds's portrait of Dr Johnson (

Reynolds, in painting his portrait, is understood by us to be as much in awe of the lexicographer as we are ourselves, and this has affected the way in which the sitter is portrayed. The situation is quite otherwise in the case of a portrait, or ostensible portrait, such as the Mona Lisa, by Leonardo da Vinci. The priorities are reversed in this instance; the features, or some semblance of the features, once possessed by the woman referred to in Leonardo's picture, are significant only in so far as they mediate our awareness Leonardo's art as a painter:

en: that is, Leonardo is seen as responsible for the Mona Lisa's appearance, or at least, what is fascinating and compelling about her appearance from the patient/ recipient's point of view; whereas Reynolds is not seen as responsible for the compelling aspects of Dr Johnson's appearance.

zh: 通过在这个公式内部作替换——在一个其余部分相同的公式中切换艺术家与原型的相对位置——我们就能表达两种再现之间的基本差异：一种认为作用于索引的能动性最终来自艺术家（如蒙娜丽莎的情形），另一种则似乎以原型为能动性的最终来源（如约翰逊博士的情形）。因此我们的公式旨在提供可以按需要调整和变换的模型，以便区分各项之间施动者／受动者关系的所有可能组合。
en: By making substitutions within the formula—in this case, by switching the relative positions of the artist and the prototype in an otherwise identical formula-we can express the basic difference between representations in which the ultimate source of agency over the index is attributed to the artist (as in the Mona Lisa case), and those representations in which ultimate agency seems to rest with the prototype (as in the case of Dr Johnson). Our formulae are designed therefore to provide models which can be manipulated and transformed at will, so as to discriminate between all possible combinations of agent/ patient relations between terms.

zh: 这对应于这样一种情境：艺术家相对于索引是“受动者”，索引中介他与接受者之间的“受动者”关系；然而就图像的指称而言，他是施动者。这类公式中的“接受者-A”一般指作为赞助人或发起者的接受者。“艺术家-P”意味着我们从索引中溯因出的是艺术家对赞助人加于他的要求的被动接受；另一方面，索引的原型（在这个公式中）是艺术家行使能动性所提供的。什么样的现实索引可能引发以这种方式“分布”的能动性溯因？嗯，考虑如下学校情境：教师（接受者—赞助人）走进来，说：“今天，同学们，我要你们每个人都凭自己的想象画点东西，所以动手吧！……”小艺术家们于是奉命开始创作他们的索引。所得的艺术品索引教师的能动性；若非教师给班级下达指示，这些想象性艺术练习没有一个会存在。学校美术反映儿童作为“受动者”的生活，至少过去是这样。学校里的美术作品是奉成人之命制作的，以取悦他们、或至少不冒犯他们。从人类学上说，学校艺术的重要特征在于它告诉我们掌权成人与受其监护儿童之间的社会关系。另一方面，教师这一次并没有告诉班上的孩子画什么，所以尽管每个孩子都试图画出让教师满意的东西（不画“不雅”的人物、不画流血的尸体、多画山景和不甚符合植物学的花卉图），每个孩子都不得不在“受动者”角色内行使能动性。因此上述公式的要求就得到满足。
en: This corresponds to a situation in which the artist is a ‘patient' with respect to the index, which mediates the ‘patient' relationship he has with the recipient; with respect to the reference of the image, however, he is the agent. ‘Recipient-A' in a formula like this, means generally the recipient as patron or prime mover. ‘Artist-P' implies that the artist's passive acceptance of the patron's demands on him are what we abduct from the index; on the other hand, the prototype of the index (in this formula) is contributed by the agency of the artist. What kind of real-life index might motivate the abduction of agency ‘distributed' in this way? Well, consider a school situation as follows; the teacher (recipient patron) enters, and says: ‘today, class, I want you all to paint something from your own imaginations, so get busy! . . .'. The young artists accordingly set to and produce their indexes under orders. The resulting works of art index the agency of the teacher; but for the teacher giving the class its instructions, none of these exercises in imaginative art would exist. School art is, or at least was, indicative of the lives children lead as ‘patients'. School art is produced at the behest of adults, so as to please them, or at least not offend them. Anthropologically speaking, the important feature of school art is what it tells us about the social relations between adults in authority and the children in their charge. On the other hand, the teacher has not, on this occasion, told the children in the class what to represent, so although each child attempts to paint something which will be acceptable to the teacher (no ‘rude' people, no bleeding corpses, plenty of views of mountains and botanically questionable flower-pieces), each is obliged to exercise agency within the ‘patient' role. Hence the requirements of the formula given above would be met.

zh: 最后，让我们再取一个实例，这次是 艺术家-A ⟶ [索引-P → [原型-P → [接受者-P]]]。这一公式把艺术家显示为唯一施动者，对索引行使能动性，索引中介他对原型的能动性，原型又中介他对接受者的能动性。可以说，这是“艺术天才”公式。一个恰当的例子可能由萨尔瓦多·达利的作品提供，他是一位在崇拜的公众面前把“天才”角色扮演到极致的画家。达利的任何一幅画（例如《记忆的永恒》，又名《软表》）都可以、而且经常主要被视为他作为画家之能动性的索引。达利画作精湛的技法凸显了他作为画家的能动性。此外，达利作品的原型（再现内容）据说是达利私人的梦境世界，而非他努力再现的真实外部世界中的任何东西。因此原型相对于达利作为索引生产者的能动性处于“受动者”位置。《记忆的永恒》是达利的一幅超现实主义“自画像”。最后，接受者不是赞助人，而是被动观者，达利以一副十足的贵族式蔑视看待他们。达利艺术的目标是通过颠覆和扰乱观者的小资产阶级感受力来支配观者。像达利这样施虐的、专横的艺术家，不把艺术瞄准同为施虐者的公众，而是瞄准一个以被冒犯为乐、热爱压迫者的受虐公众。因此在这里把接受者标示为“受动者”是恰当的。
en: Finally, let us take another instance, this time of Artist-A ⟶ [Index-P → [Prototype-P → [Recipient-P]]]. This formula shows the artist as sole agent, exercising agency over the index, which mediates his agency over the prototype, which in turn mediates his agency over the recipient. This, so to speak, is the ‘artistic genius' formula. A suitable example might be provided by the work of Salvador Dali, a painter who played the ‘genius' role to the hilt, before an adoring public. Any painting by Dali (e.g. The Persistence of Memory a.k.a. The Soft Watch) can be seen, and frequently is seen, primarily as an index of his agency as a painter. Dali's painterly agency is emphasized by the brilliant technical finish of his work. Moreover, the prototype of a Dali (the representational content) is supposedly Dali's private dream-world, rather than anything in the real, external, world, which he was striving to represent. Hence the prototype is in the ‘patient' position, relative to Dali's agency as the producer of the index. The Persistence of Memory is a Surrealist ‘self-portrait' of Dali. Finally, the recipient is not a patron, but a passive spectator, whom Dali regarded with a fine show of aristocratic contempt. The aim of Dali's art was to dominate the spectator by subverting and deranging his or her petit bourgeois sensibilities. Sadistic, domineering artists like Dali do not target their art at a public of fellow-sadists, but at a masochistic public which revels in being outraged and loves the oppressor. Hence it is appropriate to indicate the recipient as a ‘patient' here.

zh: 据我费力的计算，把索引、艺术家、接受者、原型组合成对应于[

-2]所示树状结构的施动者—受动者关系，并遵守“索引”必须作为首要施动者或首要受动者出现的规定，可以导出三十六个公式。不过，读者会松一口气地得知，我不打算为其中每一个都提供实例，尽管也许能找到例子。但这样做意义不大；这些公式只是提供一种手段，用以区分艺术品周边施动者—受动者关系的不同分布；它们不预测也不解释这些分布。而且，正如我们将看到的，为了给非常常见的艺术能动性模式提供恰当模型，我们需要增加一些进一步的细化。尤其没有任何经验理由要求我们四个基本“项”中的任何一个在给定公式中只出现一次。我们已经知道这一点，因为在前面讨论的自反能动性实例中，同一个项必然出现两次，作为施动者或受动者。但在结束四项公式及其相关树状结构的讨论之前，还有一些进一步的要点需要讨论。
en: There are, according to my laborious calculations, thirty-six formulae which can be derived by combining index, artist, recipient, and prototype in agent patient relations corresponding to the tree-structures shown in

–2, and keeping to the stipulation that the ‘index' has to figure either as the primary agent or as the primary patient. However, the reader will be relieved to be told that I do not intend to provide instances of every single one of them, though perhaps examples might be found. There would be little point in doing so though; these formulae just provide a means of distinguishing between different distributions of agent patient relations in the vicinity of works of art; they do not predict them or explain them. And, as we will see, in order to provide appropriate models for very common modes of artistic agency, we need to add some further refinements. There is, in particular, no empirical reason why any of our four basic ‘terms' should appear only once in a given formula. We already know this, because in the instances of self-reciprocal agency discussed earlier, the same term necessarily occurs twice, as an agent or a patient. But before I conclude the discussion of four-term formulae and their associated tree-structures, there are some further points which require discussion.

zh: 第一个问题涉及方法；它关乎每个公式在多大程度上应被理解为对一个“客观上”不同情境的图式描述，而非对同一个情境的不同“视角”。我们可以方便地参照已经引入的两个例子来讨论这个问题：达利的《软表》和列奥纳多的《蒙娜丽莎》，对后者我给出了公式：
en: The first of these is methodological; it concerns the degree to which each formula is to be understood as a schematic description of an ‘objectively' different situation, as opposed to a different ‘perspective' on a situation which remains the same. We can conveniently discuss this problem with reference to two examples that have already been introduced; Dali's Soft Watch and the Mona Lisa, by Leonardo, for which I gave the formula:

zh: (列奥纳多) [[[艺术家-A] → 原型-A] → 索引-A] ⟶ 接受者-P
en: (Leonardo) [[[Artist-A] → Prototype-A] → Index-A] ⟶ Recipient-P

zh: 而对达利，我给出的公式是：
en: while for the Dali I gave the formula:

zh: (达利) 艺术家-A ⟶ [索引-P → [原型-P → [接受者-P]]]
en: (Dali) Artist-A ⟶ [Index-P → [Prototype-P → [Recipient-P]]].

zh: 这两个公式之间的差异，是由“索引”项从《蒙娜丽莎》公式中标示主要施动关系的箭头（⟶）的左侧移到《软表》公式中的右侧而产生的。我绝不主张这一移动源于这两幅画中任何一幅存在的客观特征。这一移动是对围绕这些画的关系关联域的“视角”移动。“达利”公式把聚光灯打在艺术家身上；从观察者的观点看，他本人及其活动都清晰可见，成为关注的主题。情境中所有其他因素都被视为从属于他；展出的画布首先是“达利作品”——他那强势人格留下的被动印记，中介他对公众的能动性。从人类学上说，个人崇拜是从这一视角看最显著的社会互动。然而，我们可以拒绝采取这一观点；转而聚焦于作为显在施动者的达利画作，而非作为我们注意焦点的画家达利。那么我们的视角就对应于《蒙娜丽莎》公式。《记忆的永恒》是一幅杰出的画，值得独立于围绕达利的个人崇拜而受到严肃的艺术史考量。反过来，有理由怀疑列奥纳多不仅对他的画布行使能动性，而且还发起了一种他自己的个人崇拜，这是他的历史遗产的一部分，正如达利的情形。从达·芬奇崇拜者的观点看，《蒙娜丽莎》在主题上不被感知为一幅图像，而是作为半神创造性英雄列奥纳多的神圣遗物。因此我们也许可以从这一替代视角、用我们先前用于达利的公式，重新描述围绕《蒙娜丽莎》的关系关联域。
en: The difference between these two formulae is produced by a shift of the ‘index' term from the left of the focal agency arrow (⟶) in the Mona Lisa formula, to the right, in the Soft Watch formula. It is far from being my contention that this shift results from any objective feature present in either of these paintings. The shift is a shift in ‘perspective' on the nexus of relationships around these paintings. The ‘Dali' formula puts the spotlight on the artist; his person and activity are out in the open and thematic from the observer's point of view. All other factors in the situation are seen as subordinated to him; the canvases on show are, above all, ‘Dalis'-passive impressions of his dominant personality, mediating his agency over his public. The cult of personality is, anthropologically speaking, the salient social transaction from this perspective. We could, however, refuse to take this point of view; focusing instead on Dali's painting as the overt agent, rather than on Dali the painter as the focus of our attention. Then our perspective would correspond to the Mona Lisa formula. The Persistence of Memory is a distinguished painting, deserving of serious art-historical consideration independently of the cult of personality surrounding Dali. Conversely, there is reason to suspect that Leonardo exercised agency not only over his painted canvases, but also in initiating a cult of personality of his own, which is part of his historical legacy, just as in the Dali case. From the point of view of the da Vinci cultists, the Mona Lisa is thematically perceived, not as an image, but as a sacred relic of Leonardo, the semi-divine creative hero. So we may be at liberty to redescribe the nexus of relations surrounding the Mona Lisa from this alternative perspective, in terms of the formula we previously used for Dali.

zh: 如果我们作这些替换或重新描述，什么改变了、什么保持不变？在某种意义上，把索引置于施动者或受动者位置之间的差异是修辞性的；事实上类似于 (i)“列奥纳多·达·芬奇画了《蒙娜丽莎》”与等价的“被动”结构 (ii)“《蒙娜丽莎》由列奥纳多·达·芬奇绘制”之间的修辞差异。虽然两句都把《蒙娜丽莎》的创作归于列奥纳多，但只有在 (i) 中列奥纳多是句子的主语或话题，而在 (ii) 中《蒙娜丽莎》是。句子 (i) 对应于索引位于“能动性”箭头右侧的公式，而句子 (ii) 对应于能动性可归于索引的情形，如：“《蒙娜丽莎》（列奥纳多·达·芬奇画的）在我小时候把我震撼了”。事实上，被动结构很大程度上就是为用于这类关系从句而存在的。这个句子的意思与列奥纳多·达·芬奇作主语的句子不完全相同：“列奥纳多·达·芬奇（画了《蒙娜丽莎》的那位）在我小时候把我震撼了”。基本信息相同，但不同的句法模式意味着对世界明显不同的“分析”。哪种分析恰当，是社会或心理判断的问题。在此基础上我要论证，虽然把索引视为首要施动者或首要受动者的决定是一个不由情境“基本事实”决定的选择问题，但这一选择并非任意，而是由社会学或心理学上关于恰当性的考虑所驱动。
en: What changes, and what remains the same, if we make these substitutions or redescriptions? In a sense, the difference between placing the index in the agent or patient position is rhetorical; akin, in fact, to the rhetorical difference between (i) ‘Leonardo da Vinci painted the Mona Lisa' and the equivalent 'passive' construction (ii)'The Mona Lisa was painted by Leonardo da Vinci'. Although responsibility for the Mona Lisa is in both cases attributed to Leonardo, only in (i) is Leonardo the subject or topic of the sentence, whereas in (ii) the Mona Lisa is. Sentence (i) corresponds to the formula in which the index comes to the right of the 'agency' arrow, whereas sentence (ii) corresponds to the case where agency can be attributed to the index, as in: 'The Mona Lisa (which was painted by Leonardo da Vinci), blew my mind away when I was a kid'. In fact, passive constructions largely exist for use in relative clauses like this. This sentence does not mean quite the same as one in which Leonardo da Vinci figures as main subject: 'Leonardo da Vinci (who painted the Mona Lisa) blew my mind away when I was a kid'. The same basic information is there, but a different syntactical pattern implies a distinctly different 'analysis' of the world. Which analysis is the appropriate one is a matter of social or psychological judgement. On this basis I would argue that although the decision to treat the index as primary agent or primary patient is a matter of choice not dictated by the 'basic facts' of a situation, the choice is not arbitrary, but is motivated by sociological or psychological considerations of appropriateness.

zh: 下一点与此相关。在我提出的公式中，已规定索引始终是焦点或中心的施动者或受动者。“中心”意味着“可见的”“显在的”“直接的”；它不一定意味着“最重要的”。尤其当索引是施动者时，它不意味着“拥有最多原初能动性”，当它是受动者时，不意味着“能动性的终极对象”。在一个“列奥纳多”类型的公式中：
en: The next point is related to this. In the formulae I have presented, it has been stipulated that the index is always focal or central agent or patient. ‘Central' means ‘visible', ‘overt', ‘immediate'; it does not necessarily mean ‘most important’. In particular, it does not mean, ‘most endowed with original agency' when the index is the agent, or ‘ultimate object of agency' when it is the patient. In a formula of the ‘Leonardo' type:

zh: [[[艺术家-A] → 原型-A] → 索引-A] ⟶ 接受者-P
en: [[[Artist-A] → Prototype-A] → Index-A] ⟶ Recipient-P

zh: 列奥纳多作为艺术家，远在首要能动性箭头的左侧，而在这个情形中首要能动性是索引对观者的能动性，观者的心智正被影响，从而使他后来说“《蒙娜丽莎》，列奥纳多·达·芬奇画的，在我小时候令我大为震撼”。列奥纳多创作出画中女士的容貌，并把它呈现在索引里，因而是那位“隐藏的施动者”，要经过两重中介才能通达：首先经由索引，其次经由索引中所再现的女士的外貌。列奥纳多像上帝，自身不可见，但经由其作品可见。人类学家对这类事情会非常熟悉。作为一个美拉尼西亚研究者，我发现美拉尼西亚关于（某物的）“基”或“根”的习语在此涌上心头。美拉尼西亚人用这一习语指某物的终极原因或起源。例如在一个猪节上，数百人聚集互相进行猪交换，每个人似乎都受自己的利益和交换伙伴关系驱动，但会有一两位领袖人物（如翁卡，A. Strathern 1971 中芒特哈根部落著名的“大人物”）被挑出作为该场合的基人（base-men）或根人（root-men），他们的首要意志与能动性不仅体现在他们自己作为猪交换者的行为中，也体现在在场所有其他人所表现的意志与能动性行为中。
en: Leonardo, as artist, is well to the left of the arrow of primary agency, which, in this case, is the agency of the index over the spectator, whose mind is being affected, thereby causing him later to remark ‘the Mona Lisa, which was painted by Leonardo da Vinci, blew my mind away when I was a kid'. Leonardo, via his origination of the appearance of the lady in his picture, and his representation of this appearance in the index, is the ‘hidden agent' to whom access is gained at two removes, primarily via the index, and secondarily via the appearance of the lady represented in the index. Leonardo is like God, invisible himself, but visible via his works. Anthropologists will be very familiar with this kind of thing. As a Melanesianist, I find the Melanesian idiom of the ‘base' or ‘root' (of something) springing to mind here. This idiom is used by Melanesians to indicate the ultimate cause or origination of something. At a pig-festival, for instance, where hundreds of people congregate to conduct pig-exchanges with one another, each seemingly motivated by their own interests and exchange partnerships, one or two leading men (such as Onka, a famous ‘big man' of the Mount Hagen tribes in A. Strathern 1971) will be singled out as the base-men or root-men of the occasion, those whose primary will and agency is manifested, not just in their own acts as pig-exchangers, but in the acts of will and agency manifested by everybody else present as well.

zh: 在上面给出的公式中，列奥纳多·达·芬奇是基人或根人，因为即使首要施动者是索引（他的能动性经两重中介从中被溯因），他仍站在“起源”处。因此，图式地说，在一个带括号的表达式中：
en: In the formula given above, Leonardo da Vinci is the base-man or root-man, since even if the primary agent is the index (from which his agency is abducted at two removes) he stands at the ‘origin'. Schematically, therefore, in a bracketed expression such as:

zh: “A”处于“基”的位置，或者我们甚至可以说“低音”的位置，因为像音乐中的低音线一样，处于这一位置者借中介对所有更高层级施动。然而这一类比也许不精确，因为同一种树状结构也可以适用于受动者与施动者。于是在达利公式中，接受者——达利的公众——经由双重中介承受他的能动性：首先是他的梦境世界意象，扰乱他们平日对现实的感受；其次是他的精湛技法，它高超得近乎超自然，动摇了公众原先对（达利的）能动性的理解（见 Gell 1992b）。这就产生了逆结构：
en: ‘A' is in ‘base' position, or, we might even say, ‘bass' position, since like the bass line in music, the one in this position exercises mediated agency over all ascending levels. However, the analogy is perhaps inexact, in that the same type of tree-structure can be made to apply in the case of patients as well as agents. Thus in the Dali formula, the recipients, Dali's public, suffer his agency through a double mediation, consisting, first of all, of his dream-world imagery, which disrupts their normal sense of the real, and secondly of his technical mastery, which disrupts their preconceptions about (Dali's) agency, since it seems supernaturally proficient (see Gell 1992b). This gives rise to the inverse structure:

zh: 其中“F”是处于“基”位置作为受动者的接受者，“D”是作为首要受动者的索引。
en: where 'F' are the recipients in ‘base' position as patients, and 'D' is the index as primary patient.

zh: 没有什么阻止这类多重嵌套表达式出现在“中心”施动者—受动者箭头的两侧，如：
en: There is nothing to prevent multiple-nested expressions like these occurring on both sides of the ‘central' agent patient arrow, as in:

zh: 我们迄今没有遇到这类公式的唯一原因是，迄今考虑的公式只有四个项，且每个（索引、艺术家、接受者、原型）只出现一次。但这一限制绝非规定。例如，接受者很容易出现两次，一次作为“赞助人”，再次作为“公众”。例如，让我们假设索引是米开朗基罗的《摩西》，众所周知，它是为纪念教皇尤利乌斯二世而雕刻的。这件作品索引米开朗基罗的能动性，但他不是“发起者”；事实上，可以说这件雕刻（以及本应伴随它的“奴隶”像）部分表达了米开朗基罗作为受动者、为比他（甚至）更强大更有分量的伟大赞助人工作的经验。摩西（原型）是教皇的隐喻，而摩西在我们的神话中是典型的“基人”。因此这一索引的公式必须包含接受者两次：一次代表作为发起者、引发米开朗基罗作为雕刻者之能动性的赞助人，第二次代表仅仅是受动者的公众——他们被米开朗基罗的艺术能动性所震慑压倒，并经由它而受制于尤利乌斯二世的间接（社会政治）能动性。要表达这一点，有必要借助上标编号来区分两类接受者：
en: The only reason why we have not encountered any formulae of this type so far is that in the ones considered so far there have only been four terms, and each (the index, the artist, the recipient, and the prototype) has occurred only once. But this restriction is by no means stipulated. For instance, the recipient can easily appear twice, once as ‘the patron' and again as ‘the public'. For instance, let us suppose that the index is Michelangelo's Moses, which, everybody knows, was carved in order to memorialize Pope Julius II. This work indexes Michelangelo's agency, but he was not ‘prime mover'; indeed, it is fair to say that this carving (and the ‘slaves' which were to accompany it) expresses, in part, Michelangelo's experience as a patient, working for great patrons, who were more powerful and consequential than (even) he was. Moses (the prototype) is a metaphor for the Pope, and Moses, in our mythology, is archetypally a ‘base-man'. A formula for this index must therefore include the recipient twice; once to represent the patron who acted as prime mover, eliciting Michelangelo's agency as a carver, and secondly to represent the public who are simply patients, awed and overwhelmed by Michelangelo's artistic agency, through which they become subject to the indirect (social political) agency of Julius II. To express this, it is necessary to resort to superscript numberings to distinguish the two types of recipient:

zh: [[[[接受者-A¹] → 原型-A] → 艺术家-A] → 索引-A] ⟶ 接受者-P²
en: [[[[Recipient-A¹] → Prototype-A] → Artist-A] → Index-A] ⟶ Recipient-P²

zh: 其中 接受者-A¹ = 尤利乌斯二世，原型-A = 摩西，艺术家-A = 米开朗基罗，接受者-P² = 一般公众。
en: where Recipient-A¹ = Julius II, Prototype-A = Moses, Artist-A = Michelangelo, and Recipient-P² = the general public.

zh: 4.4　一些更复杂的树状结构：钉灵物
en: 4.4　Some more Complex Tree-Structures: The Nail Fetish

zh: 为了探索树状结构的某些复杂性，让我们考虑一类民族志艺术博物馆的参观者熟知的图像；我指的是西非刚果地区的“钉灵物”（[
]）。这些惊人的形象在形式上是拟人的，因钉入其身体的钉子而一眼可辨，这种对（半神圣）艺术品观念的侵犯，大大增加了它们在西方观者中激起的“审美”战栗——这些观者也许想知道，米开朗基罗的《大卫》若受同样对待会是什么样子。然而，这些雕刻与西方受苦受难图像之间表面的呼应是偶然的，而在其原初情境中环绕它们的实际能动性关系网络，远比不了解原有语境的审美者所能从中提取的那套浅薄的受害意象有趣得多。
en: In order to explore some of the complexities of tree-structures let us consider a type of image well known to visitors to ethnographic art museums; I refer to the 'nail fetishes' of the Congo region of West Africa (

). These startling figures, anthropomorphic in form, are instantly identifiable because of the nails driven into their bodies, a violation of the notion of the (semi-sacred) artwork which greatly adds to the 'aesthetic' frisson they provoke in Western spectators, who perhaps wonder what Michelangelo's David would look like, given the same treatment. However, the apparent rhyme between these carvings and Western images of suffering and violation is fortuitous, and the actual network of agency-relations which surrounded them in their original setting is much more interesting than the facile imagery of victimization which is all that uninstructed aesthetes can extract from them.

en: FIG. 4.4/1. Nail fetish figures from the Congo region of Africa. British Museum, London, MM023467. Musée de l’Homme, Paris. Kongo, Loango region

zh: 据传教士人类学家登内特所述——他在刚果工作之时，殖民政府正忙于铲除钉灵物，相信它们是土著叛乱的源头——这些图像在功能上本质上是司法性的；它们与西非许多地方主持法律程序的“司法面具”属于同一范畴。司法面具惩罚宣誓说谎者；钉灵物以相当类似的方式记录承诺与誓言，并惩罚违反者。据登内特说，当要制作这样一个司法灵物时：
en: According to the missionary anthropologist Dennett, who worked in the Congo at a time when the colonial government was busily engaged in rooting out nail fetishes in the belief that they were fountainheads of native sedition, these images were essentially judicial in function; they belong to the same category as the ‘judicial masks' which presided over legal proceedings in many parts of West Africa. The judicial mask punishes those who lie on oath; the nail fetish, in rather similar fashion, registers promises and oaths, and punishes those who contravene them. According to Dennett, when such a judicial fetish was to be made:

zh: 举行一次帕拉弗［会议］，决定让谁的库鲁［灵魂］进入穆安巴树、主持将要制作的灵物。挑选一个胆气过人的男孩，或者更理想的是一名勇敢无畏的好猎手。然后他们走进丛林呼唤他的名字。恩甘加［祭司］砍倒树，据说血涌出。杀一只鸡，把它的血与他们说来自树的血混合。被点名者随后死去，必定在十天之内。他的生命为津甘加所认为的民众福祉而牺牲。他们说被点名者无一不死……人们在这些灵物（津基奇·姆博武）面前经过，呼唤灵物：如果他们做了或将要做某事，就杀死他们。另一些人去找灵物，坚持要求灵物杀死某个已对他们或将对他们造成可怕伤害的人。当他们宣誓并提出要求时，一枚钉子被钉入灵物，就他们而言帕拉弗［事务］就此了结。其余的事由那个在砍树时牺牲了生命之人的库鲁负责。（R. Dennett 1906: 93）
en: A palaver [meeting] is held, and it is decided whose Kulu [soul] it is that is to enter into the Muamba tree and to preside over the fetish to be made. A boy of great spirit, or else, above all, a great and daring hunter, is chosen. Then they go into the bush and call his name. The Nganga [priest] cuts down the tree, and blood is said to gush forth. A fowl is killed and its blood mingled with the blood that they say comes from the tree. The named one then dies, certainly within ten days. His life has been sacrificed for what the Zinganga consider the welfare of the people. They say that the named one never fails to die ... People pass before these fetishes (Zinkici Mbowu) calling on them to kill them if they do, or have done, such and such a thing. Others go to them and insist upon their killing so and so, who has done, or is about to do them some fearful injury. And as they swear and make their demand, a nail is driven into the fetish, and the palaver [business] is settled so far as they are concerned. The Kulu of the man whose life was sacrificed upon the cutting of the tree sees to the rest. (R. Dennett 1906: 93)

zh: 这一仪式序列与恩登布人用渗血的穆库拉树制作安基希小像之间有明显的共鸣（见上文3.2节）。在结构上，情境是 [[[[艺术家-A] → 索引¹-A] → 接受者¹-A] → 索引²-A] ⟶ [接受者²-P]。但这个式子远未体现情境的复杂性，树状图能把它表现得更清楚，如[

]。这一树状图包含以前未遇到的特征。首先，在“索引”（灵物）的形成中，它依次是被动的（被砍倒的树）、然后是主动的（以猎人的名字命名，并以转喻的方式导致他死亡的树）、然后又是被动的（被钉入钉子、把祈求者的请求“附着”其上的灵物）、最后再次是主动的（执行其司法功能）。索引是双重主动的，因为在其形成过程中它曾双重被动；它有能力行动（作为灵物），因为它曾被作用——既作为树，又同时作为“为民众福祉”而死的猎人。用布洛克的话说，它展示了“反弹的暴力”（1991）。其次，树状图在基部二分；钉灵物不是一个“根人”而是两个：祭司与猎人，前者负责索引作为人工制品的创造，后者负责其效力，而这一效力由猎人在宰杀猎物方面的效力所支撑。
en: There are pronounced resonances between this ritual sequence and the making of the ankishi figurines from the blood-exuding Mukula tree among the Ndembu (see above, Sect. 3.2). Structurally, the situation is [[[[Artist-A] → Index¹-A] → Recipient¹-A] → Index²-A] ⟶ [Recipient²-P]. But this hardly does justice to the complexity of the situation, which is more perspicuously shown in a tree diagram, as in

. This tree diagram contains features not encountered before. First, in the formation of the ‘index' (the fetish) it is, by turns, passive (the tree which is cut down), then active (the tree which metonymically brings about the death of the hunter whose name it bears), then passive again (the fetish which has nails driven into it, ‘attaching' the supplicant's requests to it), then, finally, active again (as it executes its judicial functions). The index is doubly active because, in the process of its formation it has been doubly passive; it has the capacity to act (as a fetish), because it has been acted upon, both as a tree, and, simultaneously, as a hunter who dies ‘for the welfare of the people'. It demonstrates, in Bloch's terms, ‘rebounding violence' (1991). Secondly, the tree diagram bifurcates at the base; the nail fetish has not one 'root-man' but two, the priest and the hunter, the former being responsible for the creation of the index as an artefact, the latter being responsible for its efficacy, which is underwritten by the hunter's efficacy in slaughtering game animals.

zh: 一个熟悉相关仪式的人走近这样一个灵物，看到的不是一个单纯之物、一个他可能或可能不以审美方式回应的形式。相反，所看到的是一个可见的结，把一束不可见的关系系在一起，这些关系扇形展开进入社会空间与社会时间。这些关系不是被象征性地指称，仿佛它们能独立于在这一特定形式中的显现而存在；因为这些关系造出了这一具体物件，使它切实在场；而正是因为这些关系存在（过），灵物才能行使其司法角色。不过，我将把这一主题的进一步讨论推迟到后面专论偶像崇拜整个主题的一章。本讨论的目的只是展示索引的“套叠”性质：它可以在单一可见形式中对象化一整系列关系。
en: An instructed person, approaching such a fetish, does not see a mere thing, a form, to which he may or may not respond aesthetically. Instead, what is seen is the visible knot which ties together an invisible skein of relations, fanning out into social space and social time. These relations are not referred to symbolically, as if they could exist independently of their manifestation in this particular form; for these relations have produced this particular thing in its concrete, factual, presence; and it is because these relations exist(ed) that the fetish can exercise its judicial role. However, I shall defer further discussion of this theme until a later chapter, devoted to the whole subject of idolatry. The purpose of this discussion is only to show the ‘involute' character of the index, which may objectify a whole series of relations in a single visible form.

en: Having disparaged the Western response which sees the nail fetish as an image of suffering, let me now turn to another example in which the sufferings of the index do genuinely connote the suffering of the prototype. However, the 'work of art' I have in mind, though belonging to the West, has so far not entered the canon of Western art. I refer to the 'Slashed' Rokeby Venus, the work of a suffragette artist, Mary Richardson (and Velazquez). This work only existed for a few months, before it was superseded by the 'restored Rokeby Venus' which can be seen in the National Gallery today (by Velazquez and the Museum's picture-restoration staff). Fortunately, Mary Richardson's version of the picture was photographed, and this image is reproduced by Freedberg (1989: 410). See

zh: Freedberg 用整章篇幅讨论所谓狂热者对重要艺术品的攻击，如玛丽·理查森（“划画者玛丽”）1914年用菜刀攻击《罗克比维纳斯》。Freedberg 指出，虽然美术馆官员在此类攻击后总是表示难以置信与沮丧，把它们归于疯狂的恶意，但攻击者心中总是确实存在强烈的宗教或政治动机。例如，国家美术馆当时最近一次被攻击的画（1978年）是普桑的《金牛犊》，且攻击者的刺击瞄准金牛犊本身，这并非偶然。当时人们对此未加留意，但 Freedberg 论证——无疑正确——这幅画被选中恰恰因为它描绘了正在进行的偶像崇拜。攻击是针对偶像崇拜的，而且有理，因为在国家美术馆，即使我们不犯十足的偶像崇拜，我们也始终接近它。
en: Freedberg devotes a whole chapter of his work to the attacks made on important works of art by so-called fanatics, such as Mary Richardson ('Slasher Mary') who attacked the Rokeby Venus with a kitchen knife in 1914. Freedberg makes the point that, though the Gallery officials always express incredulity and dismay after such attacks, ascribing them to insane malice, there always does prove to be a strong religious or political motive present in the mind of the attacker. For instance, it was not by chance that the latest picture to be attacked in the National Gallery (in 1978) was Poussin's The Golden Calf nor that the attacker's thrusts were aimed at the Golden Calf itself. Nothing was made of this at the time, but Freedberg argues, surely correctly, that this picture was chosen precisely because it depicts idolatry in progress. The attack was directed against idolatry, and with reason, because in the National Gallery, even if we do not commit full-blown idolatry, we do verge on it all the time.

en: This attack was consigned to the category of ‘arbitrary' outrages committed by schizophrenics because to admit otherwise is to drop the defences we erect between ourselves and images which move us. Freedberg says that ‘the iconoclastic act is so frightening' because:

zh: 它打开了我们可能感觉到却无法完全把握的权力与恐惧的领域。当破坏圣像者以暴力对图像作出反应、激烈而戏剧性地试图打破图像对他或她的控制时，我们才开始对其潜力有所感觉——倘若我们还没能在那道闪光中感知这种潜力的话。那闪光最终使我们对图像的艺术性视而不见。但如今我们变得更老练，因而更困惑。我们承认艺术也可以是令人不安的，于是我们绕回原点。我们学会了把令人不安的图像变成我们可以安全地称之为艺术的东西。（Freedberg 1989:425）
en: It opens realms of power and fear that we may sense but cannot quite grasp. When the iconoclast reacts with violence to the image and vehemently and dramatically attempts to break its hold on him or her, then we begin to have some sense of its potential-if we do not perceive it in the flash of light that blinds us, finally, to its art. But these days we have become more sophisticated, and thereby more confused. We allow that art can be troubling too, and we come full circle. We have learned to turn the troubling image into something we can safely call art. (Freedberg 1989:425)

zh: Freedberg 作了一个尖锐的对比：许多当代西方艺术表面上的暴力，被能说会道的批评家与收藏家捧上天（因为它是艺术）；而同一圈子的人对针对艺术品的实际暴力却作出震惊恐惧的反应。但那些因精神不稳定或强烈政治动机而克服禁忌、毁损博物馆杰作的外人，是否更明显地受制于艺术，这是值得追问的问题。正如 Freedberg 所说，这样的人被艺术“弄瞎”了，即对艺术并非真实之物这一事实视而不见。虽然在二十世纪，这类态度只能真正在极端越轨行为中表达自己，但它们是自然和基本的，而非晦涩和怪诞的。毁坏艺术品是艺术创作的反向行为，两者的基本概念结构相同。破坏图像的人也在行使一种“艺术能动性”。
en: Freedberg makes a pointed contrast between the ostensible violence of much contemporary Western art, which smooth-talking critics and collectors praise to the skies (because it is art) and the shock-horror reactions that actual violence against works of art provokes in the same quarters. But it is a moot point whether the outsiders who, due to mental instability or strong political motives, overcome the taboo against defacing masterpieces in museums, are not the more demonstrably in thrall to art. Such persons, as Freedberg puts it, are ‘blinded', by art blinded, that is, to the fact that art is not the real thing. Although, in the twentieth century, such attitudes can only really express themselves in acts of extreme deviance, they are natural and basic, rather than obscure and fantastic. Art-destruction is art-making in reverse; but it has the same basic conceptual structure. Iconoclasts exercise a type of ‘artistic agency'.

zh: 让我们考察“划画者玛丽”与《罗克比维纳斯》的案例，这是“现代”时期最著名的破坏圣像行为，而且不是出于明显的疯狂，而是出于清晰的意识形态动机。玛丽·理查森这样描述她1914年的行为：“我试图毁掉神话历史上最美丽女人的画像，以抗议政府摧毁现代史上最美好的人物潘克赫斯特夫人”（Freedberg 1989: 502）。从这段话和后来的一次访谈可以清楚看出，理查森把画中的女人（维纳斯）等同于埃米琳·潘克赫斯特，把画的“受苦”等同于潘克赫斯特夫人在狱中的受苦。换言之，这是反向的模拟巫术实例（见下文）：受害者的受苦导致再现物外貌的改变。察看攻击后《罗克比维纳斯》的照片，我们注意到最深的一道划口瞄准心脏；维纳斯被刺中了背部——这样一种死法极有政治意味。实际上，玛丽·理查森是一位艺术家，她生产了一件“新的”、现代的《罗克比维纳斯》，如今是埃米琳·潘克赫斯特的再现（象征现代女性，正如维纳斯曾象征神话中的女性）。理查森的被划破的《罗克比维纳斯》，无疑比委拉斯凯兹的旧作更有力，尽管从审美上看远不如旧作，因为这一图像带有直接见证、而非仅仅再现女性所承受或相信自己承受的暴力的痕迹。委拉斯凯兹在创造维纳斯绘画图像时行使的极度克制而超然的能动性，与理查森毁损图像、使其“死亡”对应于潘克赫斯特之死的狂乱姿态之间的对比，创造了图像与人的生命相遇并融合的空间。理查森通过“杀死”《罗克比维纳斯》、把它变成一具美丽的尸体，赋予了它从未拥有过的生命。把画修复到原状，虽然当然必要且可取，却也是重新筑起屏障的手段，防止这类图像在政治上、性上或任何其他方面过度困扰我们。
en: Let us examine the case of ‘Slasher Mary' and the Rokeby Venus, the most famous act of iconoclasm of the ‘modern' period, and moreover, one not due to obvious insanity but to clear ideological motives. Mary Richardson gave this account of her action in 1914 ‘I have tried to destroy the picture of the most beautiful woman in mythological history as a protest against the government for destroying Mrs Pankhurst, the most beautiful character in modern history' (Freedberg 1989: 502). From this and from a later interview, it is quite clear that Richardson equated the woman in the picture (Venus) with Emmeline Pankhurst, and the ‘sufferings' of the picture with Mrs Pankhurst's sufferings in prison. In other words, this is an instance of volt sorcery (see below) in reverse; the sufferings of the victim cause a change in the appearance of the representation. Examining the photograph of the Rokeby Venus after the attack, we note that the deepest slash is aimed at the heart; Venus has been stabbed in the back-a very political way to die. In effect, Mary Richardson was an artist who produced a ‘new', modern, Rokeby Venus, now a representation of Emmeline Pankhurst (standing for modern womanhood as Venus stood for mythological womanhood). The ‘Slashed’ Rokeby Venus by Richardson, is, without question, a more powerful image than the old one by Velazquez, though infinitely less aesthetic, because the image bears traces which testify directly to, rather than simply represent, the violence women endure, or believe they endure. The contrast between the supremely controlled and detached agency exercised by Velazquez in creating the painted image of Venus, and the frenzied gestures of Richardson defacing the image so that its ‘death' corresponds to that of Pankhurst create the space in which the life of images and persons meet and merge together. Richardson endowed the Rokeby Venus with a life it never possessed before by ‘killing' it and turning it into a beautiful corpse. The restoration of the picture to its original condition, though of course necessary and desirable, was also a means of re-erecting the barrier which prevents such images troubling us unduly, politically, sexually, or in any other way.
